description.text: Pinnacle West is an investor-owned electric utility holding company based in Phoenix, Arizona with consolidated assets of approximately $30 billion. We derive essentially all of our revenues and earnings from our principal subsidiary, APS. Since 1886, APS and its affiliates have provided energy and energy-related products to people and businesses throughout Arizona. APS is Arizona’s largest and longest-serving electric company and generates safe, affordable electricity in 11 of Arizona’s 15 counties. Our other active subsidiaries are El Dorado and PNW Power. Our reportable business segment is our regulated electricity segment, which consists of traditional regulated retail and wholesale electricity businesses (primarily electric service to Native Load customers) and related activities, and includes electricity generation, transmission, and distribution. Our reportable business segment activities are conducted primarily through our wholly-owned subsidiary, APS.

about.description_short: Pinnacle West is a holding company whose principal subsidiary is Arizona Public Service, a vertically integrated electric utility that serves 1.3 million customers across a 35,000-square-mile territory in central Arizona, including Phoenix. APS owns or leases more than 6 gigawatts of power generation capacity, including a 29% ownership stake in the largest nuclear plant in the U.S., Palo Verde. About half of the electricity that APS supplies to customers comes from clean energy sources, including nuclear.

analysis_md:
# PNW — Pinnacle West Capital Corporation
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-18. In scope (market cap $12.614B at $103.42, nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. Guidance and quarter figures are from cited search results, as noted.

## What it is
Phoenix-based regulated utility holding company whose principal subsidiary is Arizona Public Service (APS), Arizona's largest electric utility: generation (including the APS-operated Palo Verde nuclear station, the largest nuclear plant in the US), transmission and distribution across one of the fastest-growing service territories in the country. Essentially all earnings are regulated by the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC). The model is rate-base compounding: a $10.35B capital plan for 2025–2028 (generation, transmission, distribution), weather-normalized sales growth guided at 5%–7% through 2030, and long-term EPS growth targeted at 5%–7% (search results). A rate case is pending: APS requests roughly a $611M net revenue increase (a ~14.75% day-one customer bill impact) on a 10.70% requested ROE, plus a proposed formula rate adjustment mechanism to cut regulatory lag (search results).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $5,339,939,000; net income $631,643,000; operating cash flow $1,805,095,000; capex $2,624,618,000 (tag: PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets); SBC $27,457,000 (tag: ShareBasedCompensation); D&A $969,615,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$846,980,000 = −$6.94/share** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_total_latest_fy −$846,980,000, base_oe_latest_per_share −$6.9441). Capex exceeds operating cash flow — structural for a utility spending ~$2.6B/yr on rate base, not a one-off year.
- **OE positive 0 of the last 5 fiscal years** (dcf_numbers.json): FY2021 −$631,921,000 / FY2022 −$481,991,000 / FY2023 −$656,014,000 / FY2024 −$662,904,000 / FY2025 −$846,980,000, from financials_history.csv (oe_conservative).
- Maintenance version FY2025: $937,333,000 (financials_history.csv, oe_maintenance) — positive, and that gap between the two definitions is the story: most utility capex is growth capex that enters rate base and earns an allowed return, so the conservative definition (OCF − total capex − SBC) is the harsher yardstick, and it is the sweep's base case.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): −$5.7644/share** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_per_share −5.7644195283118345, source median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; latest FY alone is −$6.9441/share). Both are negative, and the TTM figure below is more negative still, so the choice of base does not change the verdict. No TTM pin was applied — see STALE_FY below.
- Balance sheet: net debt $10,556,077,000 (dcf_numbers.json), plus lease liabilities of $3,736,951,000. Shares diluted (latest): 121,971,000, with the share count growing at a 2.45% CAGR (dcf_numbers.json, share_cagr 0.02453) — recurring equity issuance funds part of the capital plan ($1.0B–$1.2B of new equity financing planned through 2028, per search results) and dilutes per-share compounding.

## Moat: 6/10 — durable regulated monopoly, capped economics
Justification: Exclusive regulated electric franchise (Arizona Public Service) in a top-growth territory — customer growth 2.1% and weather-normalized sales +5.6% in Q2 2026, 5%–7% sales growth guided through 2030, semiconductor/large-load demand, and Palo Verde baseload — a durable, visible compounding machine. Capped at 6 because the Arizona Corporation Commission sets the allowed return (pending case requests 10.70% ROE; measured roic_proxy is only 4.09%–5.32% over FY2021–FY2025, at/below the cost of capital through the cycle), there is no pricing power beyond rate cases, and the build is funded with debt (net debt $10,556M) plus $1.0B–$1.2B of planned equity issuance on a share count already growing +2.45%/yr.
- FOR: Exclusive regulated electric franchise in one of the fastest-growing US service territories — APS customer growth 2.1% in Q2 2026, weather-normalized sales growth 5.6%, long-term weather-normalized sales growth guided 5%–7% through 2030; Palo Verde nuclear station — APS-operated, the largest US nuclear plant — gives low-marginal-cost baseload, with 20-year license renewals sought through 2065–2067; semiconductor and large-load expansion in the Phoenix metro drives commercial load growth on top of residential growth — total sales +9.6% in Q2 2026; essential, inelastic demand with a 12-year dividend growth record (fundamentals.json) and a $10.35B 2025–2028 capital plan that enters rate base and earns regulated returns once recovered.
- AGAINST: The ACC caps the economics: the pending rate case requests a 10.70% ROE and ~$611M net revenue increase with a ~14.75% day-one bill impact — recovery can be trimmed, lagged or politicized (the ACC's rooftop-solar surcharge was vacated by the Arizona Court of Appeals in June 2026); measured returns are thin: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json runs 4.09%–5.32% over FY2021–FY2025 and ROE 8.28%–10.77% — at or below the cost of capital, as regulated returns are designed to be; growth is debt- plus equity-funded: net debt $10,556M plus $3,737M lease liabilities, and $1.0B–$1.2B of new equity financing planned through 2028; share count already grows +2.45%/yr, diluting rate-base growth per share; extreme-heat / wildfire / water exposure in the Arizona service territory and Palo Verde concentration raise physical and remediation cost tails that sit with equity if recovery is denied.
- Evidence on returns (fundamentals.json, last five fiscal years): roic_proxy FY2021 4.86% / FY2022 4.09% / FY2023 4.73% / FY2024 5.32% / FY2025 5.19%; ROE 10.77% / 8.28% / 8.40% / 9.27% / 8.96% over the same years. Gross margin is not split out for this filer in fundamentals.json (utility cost-of-service presentation), so the ROIC series is the returns evidence. That is exactly the regulated profile: returns pinned near the allowed level, never well above the cost of capital — which is why the moat cannot score 7+ under the sweep's rubric despite the franchise's durability.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years (dcf_numbers.json, cap_years 9.8) — academic here, since there is no positive OE stream to fade.

## DCF — engine 5.4 final run (2026-10-18)
The final engine pass was run with moat 6 and default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 (offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp, multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25), but **the engine emits no scenario table, IV, or IRR: the normalized base OE is −$5.7644/share, so there is no positive owner's-earnings path to discount at any scenario weighting.** Tier by numbers: **F** (f_subtype: no_cash_generation — the sum of the last 3 fiscal years' OCF − capex is not positive).

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | n/a | 0.75 | Rate case trimmed hard; affordability politics cap recovery | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bear | 25% | n/a | 0.90 | Capex stays above OCF; equity issuance at the top of the $1.0–1.2B plan | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Base | 30% | n/a | 1.00 | Capex > OCF indefinitely on the $10.35B plan; OE stays negative | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bull | 25% | n/a | 1.10 | Full rate recovery plus 5–7% sales growth converts to distributable cash sooner than history suggests | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Super bull | 10% | n/a | 1.25 | Structural FCF inflection | n/a — negative base | n/a |

- **Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not computable (negative base). Tier by numbers: F.**
- Sanity check on growth inputs: the engine's blended growth is 4.83% (dcf_numbers.json: g_blend 0.048297817667792176; adjusted components rev CAGR 5y 5.83%, rev CAGR 3y 4.83%, latest rev YoY 1.74% after the share-count adjustment; raw latest rev YoY 4.20%, raw 5y/3y revenue CAGRs 8.28%/7.28%). That blend sits below management's 5%–7% EPS growth target and 5%–7% weather-normalized sales growth guide through 2030 (search results) — a conservative start, not an inflated one — but growth is irrelevant to the verdict: it multiplies a negative base. No scenario start was set below a recent print to manufacture conservatism, and none could rescue a negative base anyway.
- Recent prints (search results, for the record): Q2 2026 consolidated net income $178.6M, diluted EPS $1.43 vs $1.58 in Q2 2025, on record demand (residential customer growth 2.1%, weather-normalized sales +5.6%, total sales +9.6%); the year-over-year decline came from higher interest charges, higher depreciation on higher plant balances, and lower transmission revenue. FY2026 guidance is $4.55–$4.75 diluted EPS; Q3 2026 results are scheduled for November 3, 2026. The earnings engine is healthy — it is the capex load, not profitability, that zeroes out conservative OE.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
